mission_3.prediction: I changed the repulsion strength for social_2 from 1.30 to 0.70. I made sure to keep the settings the same for everything else. Before I changed the setting, the path refinement became stuck in an oscillation and could not complete the route. However, after lowering the repulsion strength, the refinement succeeded and produced a complete path. Reducing the strength allowed the robot's planned route to continue toward the goal instead of getting stuck.
mission_3.comparison: In A*, social_2 had the biggest minimum person clearance of 0.7621 m which is bigger compared to 0.7253 m for the baseline. The time also went from 1.6 seconds to 0 seconds. The execution time went from 46.660 seconds to 46.344 seconds. The distance traveled went from 13.2104 m to 13.1692 m. In RRT, the baseline had the biggest minimum person clearance at 1.7344 m which is also bigger compared to 1.7296 m for social_1 and 1.7322 m for social_2. Social_2  finished slightly faster at 43.272 seconds compared to 44.824 seconds for the baseline.
mission_3.recommendation: I would personally choose A* with social_2 because it reached the goal while having more personal space around the person. Its minimum clearance was 0.7621 m. Compared to the A* baseline, it had a clearance of 0.7253 m. However, these trials only tested a person standing still. They do not tell us how the robot would react if someone suddenly walked across its path or moved toward it. More testing with moving people would be needed to understand how safely the robot handles those situations.
